free_tier.stated: Node-hour allocations on a cluster of dual EPYC hosts with Instinct accelerators, awarded quarterly by proposal, reachable over SSH at hpcfund.amd.com with Slurm. The vendor states: 'Node-hour based allocations are awarded quarterly to proposal submissions supporting innovative, impactful, open-source AI and HPC research', and 'Successful proposals receive cluster access for up to one year'. The application condition: 'applicants must agree to the Cluster Terms of Use, be part of a non-profit research or academic institution, and submit a clearly defined project'. The enrollment page closes the loop: 'Membership is open exclusively to faculty and researchers at universities and research institutions worldwide. Enroll using your official academic email address - personal emails won't qualify.'

notes: Recorded as the academic half of AMD's program so the next reader does not confuse it with the 25-hour developer credit, which is a different door on a different site with a different amount. The institution condition is stated three times across three AMD pages, including the enrollment rule that personal email addresses will not qualify, which is the clearest statement of the gate found in this class. A fourth page states the cluster is reviewed by an internal team at the end of each quarter and requires an annual survey and publication notification. Worth noting for completeness: the cluster is reachable over SSH and runs Slurm, so the constraint is purely the door, not the tooling.
